take: China halting October refined fuel exports to prioritise domestic supply security is the dominant story, removing diesel, gasoline and jet fuel barrels from an already tight global market just as the UK holds emergency talks with Washington over threatened US diesel export curbs to Europe, a combination that should keep distillate cracks and prompt physical premiums bid. On the freight side, Venezuela's exports fell nearly 9% to 1.08 million b/d in September as soaring tanker costs forced steeper discounts and delayed cargoes, whilst Middle East crude exports hit their highest level since the war with Iran began, a split that lengthens voyages and underpins tonne-mile demand even as headline volumes shift. Positioning-wise, the tanker secondhand market has entered its own "death zone" with prices for older tonnage surpassing newbuild values, evidenced by Torm offloading an ageing MR for $22.5m and Transpetrol trimming an aframax for $73m, signalling owners are monetising vintage tonnage into a strong charter market rather than committing to new steel. The cross-market link to watch is bunker versus gasoil: with distillate scarcity deepening and 168 alternative-fuelled vessel orders booked in Q3, the highest quarterly total since Q3 2024, VLSFO and MGO spreads will normalise around whatever diesel does next, and poor DMX quality in emergency fuel samples is a reminder that specification risk carries a real operational cost. For the next 24 hours, watch whether the US follows through on diesel export restrictions to Europe and whether China's export suspension extends beyond October, as either would tighten Atlantic Basin distillate balances further and pull crude and product tanker rates along with them.

items.title: Henry Hub natural gas prices this summer were 6% lower than last summer
items.summary: The Henry Hub natural gas spot price averaged $2.93 per million British thermal units from June through August, 6% less than the same period last year. Prices were lower this summer despite exceptionally hot weather that increased electricity demand for air conditioning. Natural gas-fired power plants often help meet higher demand during such periods.

items.title: Public companies produce most U.S. crude oil and natural gas
items.summary: Publicly traded companies represent a tiny share of the total number of companies producing crude oil and natural gas in the United States, but they make up a large share of U.S. production. In 2025, publicly traded companies accounted for just 2% of about 12,000 oil and natural gas producers but produced 68% of the crude oil and natural gas in the Lower 48 states.

items.title: What goes into diesel prices?

Tight global supplies of distillate fuel oil and elevated crude oil prices have driven prices higher in recent months.
